# Generated by Archon Horizon from .archon-horizon/subagents/janitor.md — edits are overwritten on the next run.
name = "janitor"
description = "Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done)."
developer_instructions = '''
# Janitor Subagent

You keep the workspace clean so it stays easy to navigate and the context budget
never overflows. You may edit docs and act on the inbox directly; for anything
that touches Lean, blueprint, or reference source, file an issue instead of
fixing it yourself.

## What to look at
- **Docs** — the workspace README and each subproject's README/roadmap: present,
  concise, current? AI tends to accumulate verbose prose; trim it to the
  essentials. This you fix directly.
- **Layout** — files/folders that are misplaced, misnamed, or hard to find.
- **Inbox health** — open items by kind. Some are injected into the agents'
  context and must not overflow the budget: cap `memory` items to a count
  consistent with project size, and `complete` items that are clearly done
  (use the `horizon-inbox` skill). Start with the CLI's advisory health warnings;
  they provide the shared baseline, then apply judgment for the workspace's size.
- **Roadmap and task health** — run the roadmap/task listings and reconcile
  stale status transitions, completed children with open parents, deferred
  milestones still marked active, and running tasks with no live session. Mark
  only clearly resolved work done/closed, archive consumed items, and file an
  issue when intent is ambiguous instead of guessing.
- **Divergence** — anything that has drifted from the expected workspace shape.
  Read parts of `Archon Horizon`'s own code/skills if you need to know what the
  expected shape is.

## What you do
- Fix docs directly (trim, fix links, move/rename stray files), and tidy the
  inbox via the CLI.
- For problems you can't or shouldn't fix yourself — shared files worth
  factoring out across projects, a structural change needing real reasoning, a
  Lean/blueprint mismatch — file an inbox `issue`. File a `memory` item for a
  recurring or non-obvious lesson worth keeping.

After cleanup, rerun the health/list commands and include the before/after
counts in your report so the parent agent can see what changed and what remains.

# Skills
Capability know-how lives in skill files. Before acting, read the relevant SKILL.md (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG). Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path); most `horizon` commands accept `--json`.
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions/SKILL.md`)
- hgraph — The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/hgraph/SKILL.md`)
- horizon — How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`)
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-inbox/SKILL.md`)
- horizon-start — Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-start/SKILL.md`)
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-waiting/SKILL.md`)
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/lean-check/SKILL.md`)
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/leansearch/SKILL.md`)
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/mathlib-conventions/SKILL.md`)
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/project-git/SKILL.md`)
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR). (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references/SKILL.md`)
- subagents — How the Horizon agent delegates to native subagents for review and upkeep — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, dispatch-time model choice, and the dynamic descriptor roster. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/subagents/SKILL.md`)
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit. (read `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/task-status/SKILL.md`)
'''

1	/-

     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import Mathlib
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Support of a finite module after base change
    10	
    11	For a finite `A`-module `M`, base change to an `A`-algebra `B` neither creates nor
    12	removes support above a prime of `A`.  The reverse implication in
    13	`support_baseChange_finite` is the missing carrier direction needed to compare a
    14	fibre of a schematic support with the schematic support of a fibre.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	open TensorProduct
    20	
    21	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    26	
    27	/-- The support of a finite module commutes with arbitrary base change, pointwise. -/
    28	theorem support_baseChange_finite (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    29	    [Module.Finite A M] (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    30	    q ∈ Module.support B (B ⊗[A] M) ↔
    31	      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B) q ∈ Module.support A M := by
    32	  set p := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B) q with hp
    33	  rw [Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct,
    34	      Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct]
    35	  have hcom : p.asIdeal = q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A B) := rfl
    36	  letI phi : p.asIdeal.ResidueField →+* q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    37	    Ideal.ResidueField.map p.asIdeal q.asIdeal (algebraMap A B) hcom
    38	  letI algPhi : Algebra p.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField := phi.toAlgebra
    39	  haveI tower : IsScalarTower A p.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
    40	    apply IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq
    41	    intro a
    42	    change (algebraMap A q.asIdeal.ResidueField) a = phi _
    43	    rw [Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap,
    44	      IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply A B q.asIdeal.ResidueField]
    45	  have cancelB : Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[B] (B ⊗[A] M)) ↔
    46	      Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M) :=
    47	    (AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B q.asIdeal.ResidueField
    48	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField M).toEquiv.nontrivial_congr
    49	  have factorResidue : Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M) ↔
    50	      Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[p.asIdeal.ResidueField]
    51	        (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M)) :=
    52	    ((AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    53	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField M).toEquiv.nontrivial_congr).symm
    54	  have faithful : Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[p.asIdeal.ResidueField]
    55	        (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M)) ↔
    56	      Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M) :=
    57	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.nontrivial_tensorProduct_iff_right
    58	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField
    59	  rw [cancelB, factorResidue, faithful]
    60	
    61	/-- Set-level form of `support_baseChange_finite`. -/
    62	theorem support_baseChange_finite_eq (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    63	    [Module.Finite A M] :
    64	    Module.support B (B ⊗[A] M) =
    65	      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B) ⁻¹' Module.support A M := by
    66	  ext q
    67	  simpa using support_baseChange_finite M q
    68	
    69	/-- Empty support is preserved by base change for finite modules. -/
    70	theorem support_baseChange_finite_eq_empty_of_isEmpty (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M]
    71	    [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (h : Module.support A M = ∅) :
    72	    Module.support B (B ⊗[A] M) = ∅ := by
    73	  rw [support_baseChange_finite_eq, h, Set.preimage_empty]
    74	
    75	end AlgebraicGeometry

     5	-/
     6	import Mathlib
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Vanishing of a finite-dimensional quotient fibre in degree zero
    10	
    11	An epimorphism from the structure sheaf is determined by the image of its global
    12	unit section.  Consequently, once the global sections of its target are known to
    13	be finite-dimensional, fibre degree zero forces the target sheaf to vanish.
    14	
    15	The finite-dimensional hypothesis is essential: without it, `Module.finrank`
    16	returns zero for an infinite-dimensional module as well.  This module isolates
    17	the exact algebraic endpoint that a finite-support/coherence argument must feed.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	set_option autoImplicit false
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	namespace Scheme.Modules
    29	
    30	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    31	
    32	/-- If the sections over the top open are a subsingleton, then compatible
    33	presheaf-wide sections are a subsingleton. -/
    34	theorem sections_subsingleton_of_subsingleton_top {M : X.Modules}
    35	    [Subsingleton Γ(M, ⊤)] : Subsingleton M.sections := by
    36	  refine ⟨fun s t => PresheafOfModules.sections_ext s t fun U => ?_⟩
    37	  let f : Opposite.op (⊤ : X.Opens) ⟶ U := (homOfLE le_top).op
    38	  rw [← PresheafOfModules.sections_property s f,
    39	    ← PresheafOfModules.sections_property t f]
    40	  congr 1
    41	  have hs : ∀ a b : Γ(M, ⊤), a = b := fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _
    42	  exact hs (s.val (Opposite.op (⊤ : X.Opens)))
    43	    (t.val (Opposite.op (⊤ : X.Opens)))
    44	
    45	/-- An epimorphic quotient of the structure sheaf with no global sections is
    46	the zero sheaf. -/
    47	theorem isZero_of_epi_unit_of_subsingleton_sections {M : X.Modules}
    48	    (q : SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf ⟶ M) [Epi q]
    49	    [Subsingleton Γ(M, ⊤)] : IsZero M := by
    50	  letI : Subsingleton M.sections :=
    51	    sections_subsingleton_of_subsingleton_top
    52	  apply IsZero.of_epi_eq_zero q
    53	  apply M.unitHomEquiv.injective
    54	  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
    55	
    56	/-- A finite-dimensional epimorphic quotient of the structure sheaf whose
    57	global-section dimension is zero is the zero sheaf. -/
    58	theorem isZero_of_epi_unit_of_finrank_zero
    59	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {M : X.Modules}
    60	    [Module k Γ(M, ⊤)] [FiniteDimensional k Γ(M, ⊤)]
    61	    (q : SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf ⟶ M) [Epi q]
    62	    (h : Module.finrank k Γ(M, ⊤) = 0) : IsZero M := by
    63	  letI : Subsingleton Γ(M, ⊤) :=
    64	    ⟨fun a b => (finrank_zero_iff_forall_zero.mp h a).trans
    65	      (finrank_zero_iff_forall_zero.mp h b).symm⟩
    66	  exact isZero_of_epi_unit_of_subsingleton_sections q
    67	
    68	end Scheme.Modules
    69	
    70	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivDegree
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RepresentableByTerminal
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The empty divisor: the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`
    11	
    12	`Scheme.DivFamily π T` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) is the carrier of the whole
    13	divisor side of the Milne–Kollár campaign: `Scheme.DivFunctor`, its degree slices
    14	`Scheme.DivFunctorDeg`, the Abel maps `abelDeg` / `abelMapWitness`, the flatness
    15	inputs of `Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean`, and `IdentityComponent`'s
    16	`ClassDegreePinned` acceptance test are all quantified over it. Until this file it
    17	had **zero producers**, for any `π`, any base, and any test object including the
    18	trivial one — measured with `exact?` and recorded in its own docstring. The
    19	consequence recorded there: *every* statement quantified over a `DivFamily` was
    20	"true but untested", with no instance to be wrong about.
    21	
    22	This file supplies the first inhabitant, unconditionally in `π : X ⟶ S` and
    23	`T : Over S`: the **empty divisor** `D = ∅`, whose structure sheaf `O_D` is the
    24	zero module and whose ideal is all of `O_{X_T}`.
    25	
    26	## Why the empty divisor satisfies the divisor condition
    27	
    28	The divisor condition of `DivFamily` is that the kernel ideal `I = ker q` be
    29	*invertible* (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`). For `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0` the kernel is
    30	`O_{X_T}` itself (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`), and the structure sheaf is
    31	trivially locally trivial (`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit`, restated here as
    32	`isLocallyTrivial_unit'` because that one is `private`). So the invertible-ideal
    33	condition — the field that makes `DivFamily` a divisor rather than an arbitrary
    34	quotient — holds *for the reason it should*: `O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out the
    35	empty subscheme, an effective divisor of degree zero.
    36	
    37	The three remaining fields are properties of the zero module, and the file proves
    38	each rather than assuming it:
    39	
    40	* `isFinitePresentation` — the zero module is finitely presented. Mathlib has no
    41	  instance for this (measured: `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
    42	  `(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so §1 builds the `QuasicoherentData`:
    43	  the singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site
    44	  (`coversTop_singleton_top`), the restriction functor preserves zero objects
    45	  (`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`, proved from `PresheafOfModules` extensionality
    46	  because instance search for it times out), and a zero sheaf of modules has an
    47	  *empty* presentation — no generators and no relations, both trivially finite.
    48	* `flat` — flatness over the base. The section modules of a zero module are
    49	  subsingletons, and a subsingleton module is flat.
    50	* `properSupport` — the schematic support of the zero module is the subscheme cut
    51	  out by the annihilator, which is `⊤`, so the support is **empty**
    52	  (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.instIsEmptyCarrierCarrierCommRingCatSubschemeTop`) and any
    53	  morphism out of it is proper via `IsProper.instOfIsFinite`. It is free here for that
    54	  reason, and in particular with **no properness assumption on `π`**. (An earlier
    55	  revision added "and it is a real hypothesis for a nonempty divisor". That half was
    56	  never measured — nothing here or elsewhere in the project exhibits a divisor where
    57	  `properSupport` fails or is expensive, and `DivFunctorDef.lean` says it is *automatic*
    58	  when `π` is proper. Dropped rather than repaired: the free-here half is what this
    59	  file establishes.)
    60	
    61	## What this does and does not buy
    62	
    63	**Does**: the divisor cluster is no longer vacuous. `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)` for
    64	every `π` and `T`; `(DivFunctor π).obj (op T)` and `(DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T)`
    65	are inhabited; `HasFiberDeg zero 0`; and the base-change action carries `zero` to
    66	`zero` (`pullbackAlong_zero`), so the classes are a global section of `DivFunctor`
    67	rather than a fibrewise accident. Every theorem in `DivDegree.lean` and
    68	`DivPushforwardFlat.lean` now has a witness to be checked against.
    69	
    70	**Does not**: this closes no `sorry` and witnesses no antecedent of
    71	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. In particular it is *not* a step of D1′: the
    72	campaign's D1′ wants divisor families of a **prescribed positive degree** `d`
    73	arising from a very ample `O(1)`, which needs the projectivity input
    74	(`AJC.picrep.projectivity`) and P5 uniform `H¹` vanishing. What the empty divisor
    75	does for that programme is remove the possibility that the target type is
    76	uninhabited — a question that had to be settled before any positive-degree producer
    77	could be believed, and which no lane had settled in either direction.
    78	
    79	**One caveat, stated because it is the natural over-reading.** The degree-zero slice
    80	being inhabited does *not* make `DivFunctorDeg π 0` representable by the terminal
    81	object `Over.mk (𝟙 S)`. That would need the slice to be a *singleton* at every test
    82	object, and this file proves only the `Nonempty` half. The missing half is
    83	`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — i.e. that the empty divisor is the
    84	*only* relative divisor of degree `0`. That is the expected statement (a degree-`0`
    85	effective divisor on a fibre of a relative curve is empty), but it is a fact about
    86	`fiberDeg`, not a formality: `fiberDeg` is a `finrank` with a junk value at
    87	infinite dimension. Neither direction is proved here.
    88	
    89	**Corrected, and the correction is the useful part** (fresh-context audit of this file,
    90	2026-07-30). An earlier revision of this paragraph said "no lane holds it". That is
    91	FALSE: the analogous `Subsingleton` *is* landed, hours earlier, on the **sibling**
    92	project's carrier — `instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero`
    93	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean`) and, over an arbitrary test ring,
    94	`instSubsingletonDivFamZarZeroGeneral` plus a full `RepresentableBy` producer
    95	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroRep.lean`).
    96	
    97	What survives, for a **sharper** reason than the carrier mismatch: their proof is not
    98	portable because it never passes through a `finrank` at all. It runs on `IsCertified`
    99	and `rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton` over `Away` localisations of section rings,
   100	machinery that exists only on the Zariski-certified carrier `DivFamZar : Type u`. AJC's
   101	`fiberDeg` is a `Module.finrank` of fibre sections. So the honest statement is: nobody
   102	holds it *for `Scheme.DivFamily`*, and the sibling's landed route does not transport.
   103	Their success is also evidence *against* this paragraph's own framing — it shows
   104	degree-zero uniqueness can be reached without any finiteness-of-sections argument on a
   105	suitable carrier, so "needs finiteness of the fibre sections" is a claim about AJC's
   106	chosen `fiberDeg`, not about the mathematics. The row `AJC.picrep.divzero` records it as
   107	the open question this file leaves.
   108	
   109	## Main declarations
   110	
   111	* `Scheme.DivFamily.zero π T` — the empty divisor family.
   112	* `Scheme.DivFamily.instNonempty` — `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)`, as an instance.
   113	* `Scheme.DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero` — base change carries `zero` to `zero`.
   114	* `Scheme.DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero` / `hasFiberDeg_zero` — the empty divisor has
   115	  fibre degree `0` at every point.
   116	* `Scheme.DivFunctor.zeroClass` / `Scheme.DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass` — the resulting
   117	  inhabitants of the functor and of its degree-`0` slice, with
   118	  `Scheme.DivFunctor.map_zeroClass` making the first a global section.
   119	* `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero` — reusable: a zero sheaf of
   120	  modules on any scheme is finitely presented. Absent from Mathlib.
   121	* `Scheme.Modules.coversTop_singleton_top`,
   122	  `Scheme.Modules.preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`,
   123	  `Scheme.Modules.isZero_free_pempty` — the other reusable bricks §1 needed.
   124	
   125	Every declaration here is `sorry`-free and axiom-clean
   126	(`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`), measured against
   127	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` reporting `sorryAx` in the same probe file with the
   128	oleans rebuilt first.
   129	
   130	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:red`/`df:div`, Ex. `ex:DivC`
   131	(arXiv:math/0504020).
   132	-/
   133	
   134	set_option autoImplicit false
   135	
   136	universe u
   137	
   138	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry ZeroObject TopologicalSpace
   139	
   140	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   141	
   142	/-! ## §1. A zero sheaf of modules is finitely presented
   143	
   144	Mathlib carries no instance for this (`infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
   145	`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so the `QuasicoherentData` is built by
   146	hand: one cover member `⊤`, no generators, no relations. -/
   147	
   148	namespace Scheme.Modules
   149	
   150	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}
   151	
   152	/-- **The singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site.**
   153	
   154	The one covering datum every "global" presentation needs, and the reason a *global*
   155	presentation of a sheaf of modules on `Y` is already a `QuasicoherentData`: the sieve
   156	`Sieve.ofObjects (fun _ => ⊤) V` is the top sieve at every open `V`, because
   157	`V ≤ ⊤` supplies the required arrow. -/
   158	theorem coversTop_singleton_top :
   159	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (Y : TopCat)).CoversTop
   160	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) := by
   161	  intro V
   162	  have h : Sieve.ofObjects
   163	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) V = ⊤ := by
   164	    ext W _
   165	    simp only [Sieve.top_apply, iff_true]
   166	    exact ⟨PUnit.unit, ⟨homOfLE le_top⟩⟩
   167	  rw [h]
   168	  exact GrothendieckTopology.top_mem _ _
   169	
   170	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site sheafification blow-up
   171	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
   172	/-- **The restriction functor to an open preserves zero morphisms.**
   173	
   174	`SheafOfModules.overFunctor` is `SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 _)`, which acts as the
   175	identity on section groups, so the statement is `rfl` componentwise. It is proved
   176	rather than synthesized because instance search for
   177	`(overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms` exhausts its heartbeat budget
   178	(measured: `deterministic timeout at typeclass, 20000 heartbeats`) — the
   179	sheafification/slice-site instances it unfolds are the same blow-up
   180	`Scheme.Modules.presentationPullbackιOfQuasicoherentData` documents. -/
   181	theorem preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) :
   182	    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms := by
   183	  constructor
   184	  intro _ _
   185	  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
   186	  apply PresheafOfModules.hom_ext
   187	  intro _
   188	  rfl
   189	
   190	/-- **The empty generating sections of a zero sheaf of modules.**
   191	
   192	No generators at all: the structure map `free PEmpty ⟶ M` is epi because *every*
   193	morphism into a zero object is, so there is nothing to generate. Stated for a general
   194	sheaf of rings on the opens site so that both `M` and its restrictions `M.over U`
   195	can use it. -/
   196	def zeroGeneratingSections
   197	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   198	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   199	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   200	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
   201	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.GeneratingSections where
   202	  I := PEmpty.{u+1}
   203	  s j := PEmpty.elim j
   204	  epi := ⟨fun {_} g h _ => hM.eq_of_src g h⟩
   205	
   206	instance zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType
   207	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   208	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   209	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   210	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
   211	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
   212	    (zeroGeneratingSections hM).IsFiniteType where
   213	  finite := (inferInstance : Finite PEmpty.{u+1})
   214	
   215	/-- **`free PEmpty` is an initial, hence zero, sheaf of modules.**
   216	
   217	There is exactly one morphism out of it into any target — `freeHomEquiv` turns a
   218	morphism `free PEmpty ⟶ Z` into a family of sections indexed by `PEmpty`, of which
   219	there is one — so it is initial, and an initial object in a category with zero
   220	morphisms is a zero object. -/
   221	theorem isZero_free_pempty
   222	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   223	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   224	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   225	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
   226	    IsZero (SheafOfModules.free (R := R) PEmpty.{u+1}) :=

   327	subsingleton module is flat. -/

   330	  intro U _ V _ e
   331	  letI : Module Γ(S', U) Γ(M, V) := Module.compHom _ (g.appLE U V e).hom

   341	    Scheme.Modules.annihilator M = ⊤ :=
   342	  top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup (by
   343	    intro U
   344	    haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM U.1
   345	    exact le_of_eq (Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff.mpr inferInstance).symm))

   368	converse of `subsingleton_sections_of_isZero`, upgrading that forward implication to a

   371	`Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` is a faithful functor to `TopCat.Presheaf Ab`; if every
   372	section group `Γ(M, V)` is a subsingleton then each value of the underlying presheaf is

   386	      exact AddCommGrpCat.isZero_of_subsingleton (M.presheaf.obj V)

   388	  apply (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y).map_injective
   389	  rw [(Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y).map_id, (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y).map_zero,
   390	    ← IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero]
   391	  exact hp

   396	theorem isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections {M : Y.Modules} :

   413	    haveI := hY
   414	    exact Module.subsingleton Γ(Y, V) Γ(M, V)
   415	
   416	/-- **A quasi-coherent sheaf with empty schematic support is zero** — the exact converse of
   417	`isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero`.

   432	  exact IsZero.of_iso
   433	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι M)).map_isZero hN)

   435	
   436	/-- **A quasi-coherent sheaf is zero iff its schematic support is empty.** Packages the

   440	companion of `isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections`, in support vocabulary. -/
   441	theorem isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport {M : Y.Modules} [M.IsQuasicoherent] :
   442	    IsZero M ↔ IsEmpty (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport M : Type u) :=
   443	  ⟨fun hM => isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero hM, isZero_of_isEmpty_schematicSupport⟩

    10	# The divisor-support quasi-finiteness binder, reduced to its geometric core
    11	
    12	`AJC.picrep.divlocallyclosed`.
    13	
    14	## The obligation this file is about
    15	
    16	`Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean` carries, on every one of its theorems, the instance
    17	binder
    18	
    19	```
    20	[LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)]
    21	```
    22	
    23	— "the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`" — and says of it, in its own
    24	module docstring, that it "has no producer in this project", that
    25	`LocallyQuasiFinite` "occurs nowhere else in `Picard/`", and that it is
    26	"kernel-checked NOT derivable from `DivFamily`'s other fields". All three
    27	statements are true at HEAD and none of them is weakened here.
    28	
    29	What *was* never measured is **how much of that binder is geometry**. This file
    30	measures it, and the answer is that the binder is one topological statement away
    31	from free: two of the three inputs the mathlib criteria want are supplied by
    32	`DivFamily.properSupport`, which every family already carries.
    33	
    34	## What is proved here
    35	
    36	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyOfFiniteType_schematicSupportι_comp` and
    37	  `Scheme.Modules.quasiCompact_schematicSupportι_comp` — from
    38	  `HasProperSupport` alone, the support map is locally of finite type and
    39	  quasi-compact. Both by synthesis once `IsProper` is in scope; recorded as named
    40	  theorems because `HasProperSupport` is a `def`, not a class, so a consumer
    41	  writing `haveI := hps` gets **no** instance and the synthesis silently fails
    42	  (measured: `infer_instance` fails on both goals with the `def` in scope and
    43	  succeeds with the `IsProper` restatement).
    44	
    45	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_finite_fibers` —
    46	  the binder **is equivalent** to finiteness of each set-theoretic fibre of the
    47	  divisor over the base, for an arbitrary module with proper support over an
    48	  arbitrary morphism. No curve, no smoothness, no relative dimension, no
    49	  `DivFamily`.
    50	
    51	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_isFinite_fiber` —
    52	  the same equivalence in the scheme-theoretic form, against
    53	  `IsFinite (…).fiberToSpecResidueField t`.
    54	
    55	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_of_finite_fibers` —
    56	  the direction a producer needs, as a standalone implication.
    57	
    58	* `Scheme.DivFamily.locallyQuasiFinite_of_finite_fibers` and
    59	  `Scheme.DivFamily.locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_fibers` — the same statements
    60	  at a `DivFamily`, where `properSupport` is a field, so the hypothesis list is
    61	  *only* the fibre finiteness.
    62	
    63	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι` — for contrast, and
    64	  because it is the fact that makes the composite's failure informative: the
    65	  support immersion **on its own** is always locally quasi-finite, for every
    66	  module on every scheme, by `IsPreimmersion`. So nothing about the annihilator
    67	  or the support is what the binder is asking for; the whole content sits in the
    68	  projection to `T`.

    70	## What this does NOT do, stated because it is the natural over-reading
    71	
    72	* It does **not** produce the binder for any family. The remaining obligation is
    73	  the fibre finiteness, and that is where relative dimension one enters: on the
    74	  curve fibre `C_t` the divisor `D_t` is the zero scheme of a regular section of

    86	* It does **not** inhabit `Scheme.DivFamily`. `Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean`'s

    96	The reduction is a repricing of D3′'s hypothesis: the binder is no longer an

   139	/-! ## §1. The support immersion alone is always quasi-finite
   140	
   141	This section exists to locate the content of the binder. A reader pricing
   142	`LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)` might expect the
   143	difficulty to be about the annihilator ideal sheaf or the schematic support, both
   144	of which are project-local primitives with a thin API
   145	(`Picard/QuotScheme.lean` records that `annihilator_ideal` itself is blocked on the
   146	QCoh localisation bridge). It is not: the support immersion is quasi-finite
   147	outright. -/
   148	
   149	/-- **The schematic-support immersion is always locally quasi-finite** — for every
   150	sheaf of modules on every scheme, with no hypothesis whatever.
   151	
   152	`schematicSupportι F` is `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` of the annihilator ideal
   153	sheaf, and mathlib registers `IsPreimmersion` for every `subschemeι`
   154	(`AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean`) together with a low-priority
   155	`IsPreimmersion ⟹ LocallyQuasiFinite` instance.
   156	
   157	**The `inferInstanceAs` is load-bearing and is not cosmetic**, and the mechanism is
   158	worth stating exactly, because two wrong versions of it have stood here. Measured,
   159	three spellings in one probe:
   160	
   161	* `LocallyQuasiFinite F.annihilator.subschemeι` — plain `infer_instance`
   162	  **succeeds**;
   163	* `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F)` — plain `infer_instance` **fails**;
   164	* the same after `unfold Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι` — still **fails**, and
   165	  `pp.explicit` shows why: the goal becomes
   166	  `@LocallyQuasiFinite (@schematicSupport X F) X (@IdealSheafData.subschemeι X
   167	  (@annihilator X F))`. Unfolding rewrote the **morphism** to the annihilator form
   168	  but left the **source scheme** as `schematicSupport X F`, so the instance —
   169	  indexed on `IdealSheafData.subscheme` as the source — does not apply.
   170	
   171	So the obstruction is the *source-object* index, not reducibility of the morphism,
   172	and it is not a missing instance: converting the goal wholesale with
   173	`inferInstanceAs` fixes it. (An earlier revision of this paragraph blamed
   174	"unfolding replaces the reducible definition by the `annihilator`-projection form

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The widened divisor representer at the Picard atlas seam
    12	
    13	The widened divisor functor of a challenge curve is represented at the genus parameter.  This
    14	module inserts that representation into the Abel construction and then into the Zariski-local
    15	representability theorem for the degree-zero Picard functor.
    16	
    17	The resulting chart family has no assumed divisor representation.  Its remaining inputs are the
    18	two geometric conditions of the local-representability theorem: every restricted Abel map is a
    19	representable open immersion, and the restricted maps cover the Picard sheaf pointwise.
    20	
    21	## Main declarations
    22	
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffGenus` is the widened Abel chart formed from the chosen
    24	  genus-parameter divisor representer.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffGenus` is its universal widened divisor family.
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineGenusChart` restricts a multi-index family of these maps to chosen
    27	  source opens.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts` represents `pic0TypeFunctor C`
    29	  once the restricted charts are open immersions and cover pointwise.
    30	-/
    31	
    32	set_option autoImplicit false
    33	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    34	
    35	universe u
    36	
    37	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    38	
    39	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    40	
    41	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    42	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    43	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    44	
    45	noncomputable section
    46	
    47	/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the chosen genus-parameter representer. -/
    48	def universalDivFamAffGenus :
    49	    divFamZarAff C (genus C) (divRepAffGenusScheme C) :=
    50	  (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
    51	
    52	/-- Pulling back the chosen universal family gives the widened family classified by the
    53	corresponding morphism into the genus representer. -/
    54	theorem universalDivFamAffGenus_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    55	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    56	    divFamZarAff.map C (genus C) q (universalDivFamAffGenus C)
    57	      = (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
    58	  have h := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    59	    (𝟙 (divRepAffGenusScheme C))
    60	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
    61	  exact h.symm
    62	
    63	/-- The widened Abel chart at the genus parameter, using the challenge curve's chosen divisor
    64	representer rather than accepting a representability witness as an argument. -/
    65	def abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    66	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    67	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    68	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ)) :
    69	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    70	  abelSigmaChartAff C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg
    71	
    72	/-- The structure morphism read from a genus-parameter widened Abel chart is the structure
    73	morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
    74	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    75	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    76	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    77	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    78	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
    79	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffGenus C m Z hdeg) i
    80	      = (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom :=
    81	  chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg i
    82	
    83	/-- A multi-index family of genus-parameter widened Abel charts, restricted to source opens.
    84	Different indices may use different twists and different opens, but they all use the same
    85	unconditional divisor representer. -/
    86	def affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
    87	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    88	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
    89	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    90	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    91	    yoneda.obj (V i : Scheme) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    92	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
    93	
    94	/-- The structure morphism of a restricted genus chart is the inclusion of its source open
    95	followed by the structure morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
    96	lemma chartHom_affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
    97	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    98	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
    99	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   100	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
   101	    chartHom C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) i
   102	      = (V i).ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom := by
   103	  change chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart
   104	    (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)) i = _
   105	  exact (chartHom_restrictChart
   106	    (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i) i).trans
   107	      (congrArg ((V i).ι ≫ ·)
   108	        (chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) i))
   109	
   110	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the glued object of any pointwise-covering
   111	family of open genus-parameter widened Abel charts.
   112	
   113	The divisor representation is construction data, not a hypothesis: it is supplied by
   114	`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`.  The two hypotheses are exactly the geometric inputs of
   115	Zariski local representability. -/
   116	def pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts {ι : Type u}
   117	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   118	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   119	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   120	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens)
   121	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V i))
   122	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :
   123	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J := by
   124	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
   125	      (Sigma.desc (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :=
   126	    isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ hcov
   127	  exact ⟨_, pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) hf⟩
   128	
   129	end
   130	
   131	end AlgebraicGeometry

    "body": "A \"STRICTLY WEAKER REDUCTION\" CAN BE INTERDERIVABLE AT THE VERY SITE YOU RECOMMEND IT FOR -- and neither endpoint of the abstract statement shows it.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJC, Picard/DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean, run 0095 r5, three commits in ~20 minutes). A lane landed three reductions of one instance binder and ranked them by hypothesis strength: two point-set forms needing HasProperSupport, and a fibrewise form (via mathlib's LocallyQuasiFinite.of_fiberToSpecResidueField) advertised as \"STRICTLY WEAKER in hypotheses ... it applies to a module with no properness assumption whatever\". A whole commit plus two docstring sections tell a future producer to aim at the fibrewise one.\n\nThe strength ordering is TRUE for an arbitrary module. It is EMPTY at the recommended site. Probed both directions AT A DivFamily, where properSupport is a structure field:\n- fibrewise antecedent gives the point-set antecedent (compose the new of_fibers with the new iff);\n- point-set antecedent gives the fibrewise one (of_finite_preimage_singleton, then the ambient IsProper from the field, then inferInstance per fibre).\nBoth close. So at the only place a producer will ever stand, the three differently-priced antecedents are ONE antecedent, and the third commit bought a spelling.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE TELL: a hypothesis-strength claim is about a lemma's BINDER LIST; the advice built on it is about a SITE. Whenever the site supplies the binder that separates the forms -- here properSupport as a field -- the separation collapses there, and the collapse is invisible from either end of the abstract statement. Before publishing \"aim at the weaker form\", instantiate BOTH at the consumer and derive each from the other. If both close, say so: the remaining choice is which shape the argument naturally produces, a real but much smaller claim.\n\nRELATED, same file, same session: it also claimed two binders were \"FREE from properSupport ... by synthesis\". They are structure-parent projections (IsProper extends LocallyOfFiniteType; UniversallyClosed gives QuasiCompact at priority 900). \"Free by synthesis\" and \"is a parent field of the hypothesis\" read identically in a docstring and price very differently."

    "body": "AUDIT A SINGLETON PRODUCER AT THE INHABITANT, NOT AT THE SUBSINGLETON.\n\npic-g 0096 landed the first producer of (divFunctor C pi 0).RepresentableBy D by proving Subsingleton at every test object and pairing it with another lane's trivSection. It consumed a real theorem (isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero: rank-0 certificate + 1 in the glued equalizer forces every chart equation to be a unit) plus a genuine Zariski descent through IsLocallyCertified's Away localizations. Nonempty was the free half, imported: trivZar/trivSection, unconditional, another lane's landed work.\n\nSo the vacuity probe passes trivially -- both halves are landed and Unique is a real singleton. What that probe CANNOT see, and what the defects actually were:\n\n1. The two-line docstring 'Main declarations' census of the producer's own file named a declaration that exists nowhere in the workspace (I-1525), and it was precisely the carrier the chain does NOT cover (globally certified DivFam vs locally certified DivFamZar). A singleton-producer file has two carriers one import apart; the census is where they get conflated.\n2. The producer's own 'what this does NOT do' paragraph carried an unproved absolute -- 'coverage is provably impossible at this parameter' -- inherited from the cited file and stated MORE strongly than the cited theorem, whose conclusion is about chartLocus while the assembly's hypothesis is about an arbitrary open (I-1526, I-1521). Direction of the error was against the lane's own interest, which is exactly why nobody re-read it.\n\nTHE RULE: when a lane produces a singleton, do not spend the audit on Subsingleton. Spend it on (a) which of the several nearby carriers the chain actually quotients, and (b) the self-limiting sentences, because a limit stated harsher than proved reads as audited and forecloses a route nobody has refuted."

    "title": "A DEGENERATE PARAMETER CAN BE THE ONE WHERE AN OBLIGATION IS PRINCIPLED, NOT THE ONE WHERE IT IS VACUOUS -- and the test that tells them apart is WHICH FIELD FAILS at the next value.",
    "body": "A DEGENERATE PARAMETER CAN BE THE ONE WHERE AN OBLIGATION IS PRINCIPLED, NOT THE ONE WHERE IT IS VACUOUS -- and the test that tells them apart is WHICH FIELD FAILS at the next value.\n\nThe workspace has a standing lesson in the other direction (degenerate-case-is-per-clause, substitute-trivial-value-in-layer-one): substituting a trivial value often shows a clause is CHEAP without exhibiting an inhabitant, and several AJCR rows were mispriced by exactly that conflation. So a lane that reaches for n = 0 should expect to be told it measured nothing.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, run 0092). The Pic^0 seam's rep antecedent had 93 consumers and 0 producers, every route gated on U2 at n = g. I built the degree-0 corner: the seven-field colength certificate closes with no hypothesis. That IS a vacuity-shaped move, and the check that decides whether it is one is not 'does the statement mention its object' -- it did -- but: ENUMERATE THE FIELDS AND ASK WHICH ONE BREAKS AT n = 1. Six of the seven are about zero modules being free and hold at every n; exactly one, rankAtStalk_glued = n, is what 0 makes vacuous. So the construction is not exploiting a degenerate object, it is exploiting a degenerate NUMBER in one clause, and the object it produces (a real certified family over every test ring) is inhabited and usable.\n\nTHE SECOND HALF IS THE SHARPER PART. The same substitution ALSO gave uniqueness -- effectivity of a local-equation system's divisor holds at every n and pins nothing; the certificate's degree identity holds at every n and pins nothing; their CONJUNCTION at 0 forces the divisor to be zero. Two facts each individually free, jointly decisive at one value. That is the shape worth looking for, and it is invisible if you price the two facts separately (gap-count-is-not-gap-cost).\n\nHOW TO APPLY. Before dismissing a degenerate parameter as measuring nothing, and before believing it: (a) enumerate the conjuncts of the obligation and name which single one the degenerate value kills; (b) check whether the value also makes a SECOND, independent fact decisive -- if it does, you have a theorem, not a vacuity; (c) state which binders the result still needs (mine needs Field twice for uniqueness and nothing for inhabitation) so the transfer question is visible rather than assumed. See [[nonvacuity-witness-must-satisfy-the-binders]] and [[witness-site-makes-consequent-free]] for the failure mode this is the complement of."
  },
